classified.evidence: Merged 2026-09-22T21:08Z (merge 38b549d191), same day AMX was enabled in CI. h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (+370 lines): sliding-window slots move from one whole-book arena to page-aligned chunks (<=256 MiB each); page access for reclaimable slots now goes through slot_page() with a chunk index division per page lookup. The fast path for full-history-only caches is preserved by the new constexpr guard `uniform_reclaimability && !kv_slot_specs[0].retention.reclaimable()`, so hand-written models (llama, mixtral, qwen-2.5, gemma-2 via h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp uniform_attention_operations, no sliding window) see no K/V access change. h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp + src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp: all books are now created with try_create_lazy and every extend calls reserve_book_tokens -> reserve_token_range (early return when no reclaimable chunks), plus pending_book_growth accounting in the forward loop; this scheduler bookkeeping runs for all models. Sliding-window retention is emitted only by ingest (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs cache_slot_retentions when hasSlidingWindow), so the chunked path applies to ingested models with sliding layers (gpt-oss-120b, gemma-4-31b). classified.title: Keep expert overrides from advancing base placement rotation
classified.author: mitchelldalvirosen-positron
classified.evidence: File: src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp ExpertsByPlan::start_placing now saves place_on_devices.next on the first expert request and restores it before the next ordinary tensor (git diff fee11cb9ed^1 fee11cb9ed). This changes which device receives ordinary (non-expert) weight tiles that follow expert tiles: body example 'Previously, the next ordinary tile selected device 3; it now selects device 2.' It applies only when ExpertsByPlan wraps the rotated base, i.e. MoE models loaded with load_aware_expert_placement (default true, h/tron/models/config.hpp:68) AND an expert_load.json next to the checkpoint or --expert-load-profile (h/tron/models/model.hpp:838-845, 955-958). Placement runs at load time, but the resulting weight-to-device map is used during serving, so per-device load balance for MoE rows could shift. Insufficient data on whether the nightly checkpoints for mixtral / gpt-oss-120b carry expert_load.json. Body: 'this change does not meaningfully change anything'. Merged 2026-09-22T23:54Z.

classified.title: Disable wait statistics by default
classified.author: rbjarnason-positron
classified.evidence: Files: src/system/mwaitx.cpp, h/system/mwaitx.hpp, src/system/CMakeLists.txt (new option TRON_MWAIT_STATS default OFF), CMakePresets.json (only the coverage preset turns it ON; the deb preset does not). for_event_cycles() previously did count_calls++ and count_waits++ on two process-wide std::atomic<int> on every timed-wait iteration (git diff eeb72c0348^1 eeb72c0348 -- src/system/mwaitx.cpp); these are now compiled out of the .deb. Callers execute in the serving hot path on both CPUs: worker rx wait (src/pos/worker.cpp:164,306,2044-2088,2361), threading doorbell wait (h/tron/threading.hpp:755), layer wait (h/tron/models/common.hpp:1056), DMA queue delay (src/pos/dma_queue.cpp:393). Both AMD mwaitx and Intel TSX/tpause paths go through the same for_event_cycles. PR body perf claims (GPT-OSS-20B, four cards, 2048 in / 512 out): '1 user: Decode per user 286.31 → 318.53 (+11.25%), Total output 207.59 → 223.49 (+7.66%)'; '4 users: 183.95 → 196.71 (+6.94%), 421.10 → 438.54 (+4.14%)'; 'all eight paired throughput comparisons improved'. Also: 'Those updates add contention during inference.' Merged 2026-09-22T21:14Z, 6 minutes after #4505, so the first AMX-enabled nightly .deb almost certainly also carried this change. This is a strong candidate for a cross-model, cross-machine decode boost dated 9/22.

survivors.title: tron: Rebuild moe_routing in place across forward passes
survivors.author: bgamari-positron
survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-09-26 (merge 8cb45a553b). h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp: moe_routing gains reset() that clears and refills per_expert/expert_major/batch_rank_by_token while keeping vector capacity; h/tron/models/feed_forward.hpp (handwritten MoE, used by mixtral) replaces std::optional<routing_t>::emplace with in-place build; ingest/src/TronCpp.hs emits the same in-place build_moe_routing_from_indices(..., routing) for generated MoE models (gpt-oss-120b, Muse-Glimmer). Effect: removes per-forward-pass heap allocations in the routing step (worker-0 serial path). PR body claims no perf numbers: 'steady-state passes allocate nothing'. Expected gain is small and mostly in decode, where per-pass fixed overhead is a larger share. Does not touch attention, AMX, or any dense model.

votes.reason: Reachability is confirmed, not refuted. The merge 8cb45a553b (2026-09-26T03:28Z) is on origin/main with no revert (git log --first-parent origin/main). The MoE routing rebuild runs on worker 0 in every forward pass of every MoE model, unconditionally: hand-written path feed_forward.hpp mixture_of_experts::state::run calls build_routing()/build_forced_routing() which now fill the member `routing_t routing` in place (no env flag, no build option; TRON_ATTN_STATS/TRON_MWAIT_STATS irrelevant). Generated path: origin/main ingest/src/TronCpp.hs moeRoute emits build_moe_routing_from_indices(..., routing) and moeRoutingFields declares `moe_routing<N,K>` directly (the one remaining std::optional in that area is the expert_matmul_schedule field, unrelated). Attention device does not matter: routing is CPU-side regardless of FPGA/CPU attention. Models: slug mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1 is the hand-written llama.hpp plugin (config/models.yaml source: hand_authored; llama.hpp:1588 TRON_LLAMA_CONFIG(mixtral_8x7b, ... 8 experts, top-2)), tagged production; ingested-gpt-oss-120b and ingested-meta-models--Muse-Glimmer-30B are generated, tagged production. deb preset sets BUILD_PRODUCTION_MODELS=ON and BUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON, so all three are built. All three appear as nightly rows on both intel (delphi) and amd (andoria) in rows.csv. Two corrections to the audit: (1) the change first shipped in package 2026.09.27-d3ff98db (first nightly 2026-09-27; packages.json lists 2750 under that package; git merge-base confirms dbeb404f of 09-26 does NOT contain it), five days after the 09-22 step, so it cannot explain the 09-22 boost. (2) Effect is negligible, see magnitude.
votes.corrected_category: moe-routing (allocation hygiene; no kernel or attention change)
votes.magnitude_estimate: no. Saved work is small-vector malloc/free pairs on worker 0: mixtral est. ~11 pairs/layer x 32 layers ~ 350 pairs/pass (~30 us est.) against a ~100 ms decode step (8 users at ~78 tok/s aggregate) = ~0.03%; gpt-oss-120b est. <=35 pairs/layer (reserve_per = 2*8*4/128 = 0, so only touched experts allocate) x 36 layers ~ 1260 pairs (~100 us est.) against ~65 ms/step = ~0.15%; prefill shares the same fixed cost over a far longer step. Observed CI across the carrying package (09-24..26 vs 09-27,28,30 medians): decode intel mixtral +0.38%, intel gpt-oss +1.26%, amd mixtral +1.45%, amd gpt-oss +0.19%; all inside the pre-period day-to-day scatter (e.g. intel gpt-oss 120.76 on 09-25 vs 118.92 on 09-26, a 1.5% swing) and the package also carries 10 other PRs. The amd gpt-oss prefill +13.7% appeared on 09-26 (package dbeb404f), before this PR shipped.

votes.reason: The diff only removes per-forward-pass heap churn in moe_routing (the per-expert row lists, expert_major, batch_rank_by_token, and the std::optional emplace/destroy). Counting what the old code allocated per layer: 1 outer vector + one inner vector per active expert + expert_major + batch_rank_by_token. For gpt-oss-120b (128 experts, K=4, 36 layers) at the nightly batch of 8 users that is about 35 malloc + 35 free per layer, about 2500 allocator calls per decode step. tron links jemalloc (CMakeLists.txt:211-220), whose small-object fast path is tens of ns, so the saved work is est. 50-150 us per decode step against a measured step of about 66 ms (120 tok/s aggregate / 8 users), i.e. est. 0.1-0.2%. Mixtral (8 experts, K=2, 32 layers) saves even less, est. 0.03% of its 100 ms step. Prefill of a 1024-token prompt allocates larger buffers (1-32 KB each, about 5000 calls) but that is est. about 1 ms against a measured TTFT of 960-1200 ms, under 0.1%. The batch_rank_by_token memset is unchanged (clear+resize still refills). The PR body claims no perf gain. CI confirms: packages.json places #2750 first in nightly 2026.09.27-d3ff98db (merged 2026-09-26T03:28Z, after the 9/26 package head dbeb404f at 2026-09-25T14:05Z). The 9/26 to 9/27 deltas in rows.csv are inside one standard deviation on both machines: Intel gpt-oss decode 118.9 to 120.7 tok/s (sd 1.7-2.2, and 9/25 was already 120.8), prefill 978 to 982; Intel mixtral 79.39 to 79.59, prefill 814 to 811; AMD gpt-oss 125.4 to 124.7, prefill 1124 to 1137; AMD mixtral 78.92 to 78.92. The real step changes (AMD gpt-oss prefill +12% on 9/26, Intel gpt-oss prefill +8.6% and mixtral decode +1.8% on 9/29) fall in other packages. Muse-Glimmer only appears in CI from 10/01, after this PR, so it has no before/after row.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no - saved work is a few thousand jemalloc small-object calls per forward pass (est. 0.03-0.2% of a decode step, under 0.1% of TTFT), and CI shows no step at the PR's package boundary (2026.09.27) on either machine; the allocator path is identical on Granite Rapids and Genoa, so no machine difference.

survivors.author: ishapira-positron
survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-09-28 (merge 2fafaf59a6). h/tron/kernels/rope.hpp: rope_cfg gains a template parameter rope_query_scaling defaulting to none; rope() now builds the table with cfg.amplitude(pos) (= scale.attention_factor * query_scale(pos), where the default query_scale returns 1.0f) and pass_through_amplitude(pos) (= 1.0f by default); rope_table::fill multiplies pass-through lanes by the new amplitude instead of the constant 1.0f. votes.reason: Reachable runtime path confirmed. Merge 2fafaf59a6 (2026-09-28) changes h/tron/kernels/rope.hpp. The free function rope(pos, b, cfg) now builds the per-token table with cfg.amplitude(pos) and cfg.pass_through_amplitude(pos) instead of cfg.scale.attention_factor and a literal 1.0f. That rope() is called in h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp at lines 909, 912, 926 (rope_q, Q rotation) and 1022 (fill_kv_job_template, K rotation). llama.hpp is the only production plugin (h/tron/plugins/ holds only llama.hpp and mock.hpp), so every nightly model runs this on the CPU for Q and K, whether attention then runs on FPGA or CPU. The new template parameter rope_query_scaling defaults to none, and the ingest emitter ingest/src/LoopyTron.hs mkRopeCfgType never emits the query_scaling argument, so no CI model instantiates rope_query_scaling::llama4 (the PR body itself defers production use to a later branch). With the none strategy, query_scale(pos) returns the constant 1.0f, so amplitude(pos) = attention_factor * 1.0f and pass_through_amplitude(pos) = 1.0f: an exact identity that the compiler folds. Per-token work is unchanged. The other two files are a CI snapshot-marker error message (bin/ci/ingest/snapshots.py) and a test (t/t_rope_integrity.cpp), both non-runtime. votes.reason: Merge 2fafaf59a6 (2026-09-28). The only runtime file is h/tron/kernels/rope.hpp [diff 2fafaf59a6^1..2fafaf59a6]. rope_cfg gains a template parameter `query_scaling` defaulting to rope_query_scaling::none, whose rope_query_scale<none>::operator() is `return 1.0f` marked inline/const. rope() now passes cfg.amplitude(pos) = scale.attention_factor * 1.0f and cfg.pass_through_amplitude(pos) = 1.0f into rope_table::fill, which replaces the literal 1.0f in the pass-through lanes with that parameter. Short version: PR #4455 (merge 38b549d191, 2026-09-22 18:01 UTC) only changes how the sliding-window part of the KV cache (the per-token key/value store) is allocated and addressed. It cannot speed decode or prefill up, and its slowdown is far under 1%. Machine scope is both machines equally.

What the diff does on the runtime path [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp]:
- Sliding-window KV storage moves from one arena per book (a book is a group of 64-token pages, default 1600 tokens) to page-aligned chunks of at most 256 MiB, allocated when tokens first populate them (reserve_token_range). Full-history KV keeps its whole-book arena.
- Page lookup for sliding slots now goes through slot_page(), which adds one 64-bit division and modulo (pg / reclaimable_chunk_pages_, pg % reclaimable_chunk_pages_) per (slot, kv_head, page) access. The old path (slot_base) already did a storage_location lookup and one multiply. Net cost: est. 25-40 CPU cycles per lookup.
- The constexpr fast path (direct indexing via kv_blocks_alias) stays for every cache whose slot 0 is full-history. All hand-written plugins and all ingested models without sliding layers (qwen3, llama, etc.) therefore have zero K/V access change.

Who hits the new lookup: sliding-window layers run attention in software on the CPU [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1504 run_visible_in_software = sliding_window_size < illegal_sliding_window || !uses_hw]. The CPU kernel does one k<>() and one v_data<>() lookup per (page, kv_head) [self_attention.hpp:1762,1790,1932]. Only ingest emits sliding retention [ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:642,666], so only gpt-oss-120b and gemma-4-31b are affected.

Magnitude per decode step (est., from model geometry):
- ingested-gemma-4-31b-it-tp2: 60 layers, 50 sliding, window 1024 tokens (17 pages), 16 KV heads -> 8 per rank [t/data/config-gemma4-31b-wrapper.json]. 50 x 8 x 17 x 2 = 13,600 lookups x ~30 cycles = ~0.4 M cycles = ~0.13 ms single-thread est., spread over the attention worker threads. A decode step for a 31B model is tens of ms, so this is under 0.3% even if serialized.
- ingested-gpt-oss-120b-tp4: 18 sliding layers, window 128 tokens (3 pages), 8 KV heads -> 2 per rank: ~200 lookups per step. Negligible. Sliding bytes per page are ~576 KiB, so a 25-page book fits in one chunk; chunk layout equals the old layout.
- Prefill (time to first token): allocations come from a pre-mapped 1 GiB hugepage pool with power-of-two size classes [h/system/heap_v2.hpp:42-56, src/system/memory.cpp:472], so lazy chunk allocation costs microseconds and does not fault pages. Scheduler bookkeeping (reserve_book_tokens anchor walk, pending_book_growth) is per append and microsecond-scale for all models.
- Direction: every change adds work. Nothing in the diff removes work from the decode or prefill path, so it cannot be a decode TPS boost.

Machine scope: pure integer arithmetic and allocator bookkeeping; no AMX, AVX, RTM or MWAITX dependence. Intel (Granite Rapids) and AMD (Genoa) see the same effect.

One caveat, labeled hypothesis: for gemma-4-31b tp2 the sliding arena per 25-page book was est. 625 MiB (rounded to a 1 GiB allocator slot); it is now three chunks of est. 250+250+125 MiB (640 MiB of slots). The DMA footprint per book drops est. ~38%. This matters only if the nightly ran near the hugepage limit and triggered the memory pressure governor (evictions or reclamation). Insufficient data on the governor state; the nightly's /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/hugepages_free and kv_reclamation_books_released counters would confirm or reject it. No footprint change for gpt-oss-120b (one chunk before and after).

Corrections to the first pass: the "all" model tag is not justified (non-sliding models get only microsecond scheduler bookkeeping); expected effect is "slightly negative, under 0.3%", not neutral-by-assertion.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no - adds est. 13,600 integer div/mod page lookups (~0.13 ms single-thread est.) per decode step for gemma-4-31b-tp2 and ~200 for gpt-oss-120b-tp4, under 0.3% of a step and in the slower direction; prefill allocation is from a pre-mapped hugepage pool (microseconds); non-sliding models have no K/V access change. Only a memory-pressure pathway (est. 1 GiB -> 640 MiB sliding footprint per gemma-4-31b book) could exceed 1%, and that needs governor counters from the nightly to confirm (Insufficient data).

survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-09-29T01:17Z (merge 87d521bfef). h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp: moe_routing::reset() rewritten as a counting sort into one rows_ vector with expert_offsets_ (removes per-expert inner vectors and their reserve loop; rows_for() becomes a subspan). It runs once per MoE layer per forward pass on worker 0 (TronCpp.hs:3447 'Worker 0 rebuilds routing in place'). However, two facts rule it out as a cause of the reported 9/22 decode boost: (1) it merged 2026-09-29, a week after 9/22, so it can only affect nightlies from 9/29 onward; (2) the old code was already allocation-free in steady state (per_expert_ inner vectors and expert_major_ retained capacity, as the removed comments state), so the change only removes one redundant copy of batch_tokens*top_k token-slot IDs per layer, which is microseconds against a multi-millisecond decode step. Steady-state work removed is one extra write of batch_tokens*top_k small IDs per MoE layer (old code already retained vector capacity, so no allocations were saved in steady state); est. a few microseconds per forward at nightly batch sizes versus a decode step of tens of milliseconds, far below 1% for decode and prefill. votes.reason: The diff (merge 87d521bfef, h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp) changes only how moe_routing::reset() stores the routed rows. Old steady-state work per MoE layer per forward: clear E inner vectors, push_back B*K rows into them, then copy B*K rows into a flat vector (two passes over B*K rows plus a loop over E experts, no allocations because capacity is retained). New steady-state work: count B*K rows, prefix-sum over E (<= 128) offsets, build the active list over E, then write B*K rows into one vector (two passes over B*K rows plus two loops over E, no allocations because rows_ retains capacity). The element-operation count is essentially unchanged, so the delta is a fraction of an already tiny cost. For decode (B tens of tokens, K <= 8, E <= 128) one reset is on the order of 1 us est. per layer, i.e. tens of us est. per forward against decode steps of tens of ms (about 0.1% est. even if the whole reset cost were removed). For prefill (B up to thousands of tokens) one reset is about 50-100 us est. per layer, a few ms est. per forward against prefill times of seconds (under 0.5% est. even if removed entirely). The consumers (rows_for, rows_in_expert_order) read the same row order; the PR body says accessor signatures, active-expert list, and per-expert counts are unchanged, and the diff confirms it. The only savings that are real are first-pass allocations (resize of 128 inner vectors and their reserve loop), which do not affect steady-state nightly measurements. The only perf number in the PR is the unit test t_expert_routing wall time 0.468 s -> 0.438 s (config/test-benchmarks.json), a test-process timing, not a serving measurement. The code is plain scalar CPU bookkeeping with no AMX, AVX, timed-wait, or FPGA involvement, so it cannot differ between the Intel (Granite Rapids) and AMD (Genoa) machines.

The diff (git diff eeb72c0348^1 eeb72c0348 -- src/system/mwaitx.cpp) compiles out two process-wide std::atomic<int> counters that every timed wait incremented. count_calls++ ran once per for_event_cycles call and count_waits++ once per loop iteration. These counters date from 2024-08-13 (commit 639a9515cd), so their removal is a new speedup on 9/22, not a regression fix. The hot callers are model-agnostic: every thread_pool worker spins in do_work with a 10 us timed dequeue [h/tron/threading.hpp:826, timeout_ns = 10000], wait_for_layer uses a 10 us timed wait [h/tron/models/common.hpp:1016-1021], the FPGA rx thread uses a 2 us timed mbox wait [src/pos/worker.cpp:164], and the DMA ring backpressure path calls delay_ns(2000) [src/pos/dma_queue.cpp:393]. survivors.title: Merge the two single-host channel consumer kinds
survivors.author: mitchelldalvirosen-positron
survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-09-29 (26a630b483). ingest/src/TronCpp.hs removes the `SingleHostC -> "fallback_producer_t"` override in channelField, so generated MoE routing indices channels change from tensor_latch<fallback_producer_t> to tensor_latch<signaled_producer_t> (ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs updated to expect 'tensor_latch<signaled_producer_t>> indices_channel;'). The generated moeRoute loop (TronCpp.hs ~2490) already calls start_reading_at per token; with a per-item channel start_reading(0) no longer waits on the whole-phase fallback latch (h/tron/models/common.hpp:408 vs :459-462) and each start_reading_at waits its own item latch. PR body: 'if a helper has published the indices for a token but has not finished its producer phase, routing can now complete that token's readiness wait... this does not make routing construction incremental.' Attention K/V channels (qwen-3-4b, gemma-4, gpt-oss) keep prodTy, so their generated code is unchanged. Only CPU-routed generated MoE models (models.yaml moe_router: cpu: gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b) are affected; Muse-Glimmer-30B has no moe_router entry. No perf numbers claimed. Not byte-identical regeneration. Merged 9/29, so cannot explain a 9/22 step; expected effect small (routing wait granularity), direction unmeasured.

votes.reason: Reachability confirmed, but the PR is excluded as a cause of the 9/22 step by timing and by measurement. Evidence: (1) The diff is real and not byte-identical: ingest/src/TronCpp.hs channelField drops the `SingleHostC -> "fallback_producer_t"` override, so the generated MoE indices channel becomes tensor_latch<signaled_producer_t> (per-item atomics) instead of tensor_latch<fallback_producer_t> (one whole-phase latch) [git show 26a630b483, LoopyTronSpec.hs expectation changed]. (2) The path runs in production rinzler: ingested-gpt-oss-120b-tp4 is a nightly row on both machines (rows.csv: 20 intel rows, 19 amd rows); models.yaml marks it source: generated with moe_router: cpu; every lowered L.MoeRoute statement emits a SingleHostC read of the indices buffer (LivenessAnalysis.hs:458) and moeRoute codegen emits per-token start_reading_at then build_moe_routing_from_indices; `make deb` configures `cmake --preset deb -DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE=""` (GNUmakefile:510) with BUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON, so the deb regenerates the gpt-oss-120b C++ from the Haskell generator at each nightly build. No env flag gates it. (3) Timing: merged 2026-09-29 19:18 UTC; nightly package 2026.09.29-7e5085ed does NOT contain 26a630b483, package 2026.09.30-e3b289e5 is the first that does (git merge-base --is-ancestor). So the PR first ran on the 9/30 night and cannot explain the 9/22-9/23 step. (4) Measured effect at its first night on Intel (same generated code on both machines): gpt-oss-120b-tp4 decode 122.94 -> 122.25 -> 122.59 TPS (9/29, 9/30, 10/1), prefill 1062.2 -> 1065.6 -> 1065.6 tok/s: flat within noise. AMD 9/29 run was broken (73.71 TPS, TTFT 7916 ms), so the AMD 124.9 (9/28) -> 128.8 (9/30) change spans two packages and cannot be attributed; Intel places its own +1.9% step (120.61 -> 122.94) at 7e5085ed, which predates this PR. (5) Mechanism bounds the effect: worker 0 (main) skips helper kernels when n_workers > 1 (skipMainThreadSetup), so it waits for helpers in both variants; the only saving is the gap between a helper's last finish_writing_at and its finish_writing count_down, sub-microsecond per MoE layer. Attention K/V channels of qwen-3-4b and gemma-4 already used the producer latch (PerItemSingleHostC -> prodTy), so their generated code is unchanged. Hand-written mixtral-8x7b row is not generated and unaffected. Insufficient data: I did not locate the consumer of the models.yaml `moe_router: cpu` key, but the indices channel exists for every generated MoE model regardless of that key.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no. Bound: <= ~1 us saved per MoE layer x 36 layers (est.) against a ~65 ms decode step at 8 users (8 / 122 TPS), so <= 0.06% est.; measured Intel first-night change is -0.6% decode and +0.3% prefill, inside night-to-night noise, and the PR first ran on 9/30, eight nights after the 9/22 step.

votes.reason:
Short version: PR #4654 changes only Haskell code generation (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs, Tron.hs); the one runtime effect is that the MoE top-k indices channel in generated MoE plugins becomes tensor_latch<signaled_producer_t> (per-item wait) instead of tensor_latch<fallback_producer_t> (whole-phase wait). The routing step still waits for every token's indices before build_moe_routing_from_indices, so the saved time per MoE layer is only the tail between a helper's last finish_writing_at and its finish_writing (tens to hundreds of ns). CI shows no step on the first package that contains it.

Mechanism (verified in the diff and h/tron/models/common.hpp, h/tron/threading.hpp, h/system/mwaitx.hpp):
- Old path: main thread start_reading(0) waited on one fallback latch counted down by all n_workers after each finished the router kernel; start_reading_at was a no-op.
- New path: start_reading() is a no-op; the generated moeRoute loop calls start_reading_at(task_ix) for every token (TronCpp.hs moeRoute), each waiting on a per-item atomic that the host top-k kernel sets via finish_writing_at (staticStrategy already emitted finish_writing_at per item; it was a no-op under fallback).
- Upper bound on the gain: the slowest helper's loop-exit plus finish_writing() call, about 0.1-1 us per MoE layer. Upper bound on the cost: up to one extra sleep/wake per item per layer. At 8 users the decode step is about 65 ms (8 tokens / 122 tok/s), so even 10 us per layer x 36 layers (gpt-oss-120b public config) is 0.36 ms = 0.55%; realistic effect is below 0.1%. Prefill (1024 prompt tokens, TTFT about 0.96 s) adds about 1024 acquire loads per layer, about 0.01%.
- Scope: expert selection (top-k) runs on the host under both router policies (ingest/README.md:123), so the change applies to every generated MoE plugin, not only moe_router: cpu ones. In the nightly set only ingested-gpt-oss-120b-tp4 is a generated MoE model; mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1-tp2 is hand_authored (config/models.yaml:458) and Muse-Glimmer-30B's export has no MoE routing op.

CI data (rows.csv, gpt-oss-120b-tp4, 8 users):
- #4654 merged 2026-09-29 19:18Z. Package 2026.09.29-7e5085ed (head 00:21Z) does NOT contain it; 2026.09.30-e3b289e5 is the first that does (git merge-base --is-ancestor).
- Intel decode: 9/29 122.94 -> 9/30 122.25 tok/s (-0.6%), 10/01 122.59, 10/02 121.90. Intel prefill: 1062.2 -> 1065.6 tok/s (+0.3%). Both within the night-to-night spread of the preceding flat week (118.9-120.8, about +/-0.8%). The Intel +1.9% step (120.6 -> 122.9) happened on the 9/29 package, before #4654.
- AMD: the 9/29 run is unusable (mean 73.7 tok/s, sd 60.8, TTFT 7.9 s), so AMD 9/28 124.9 -> 9/30 128.8 (+3.1%) spans both the 9/29 and 9/30 packages and cannot isolate #4654. Insufficient data on AMD; the mechanism offers no vendor-specific path (see machine scope).
- Merged 9/29, so it cannot explain the 9/22 step. Separate note: #4713 (gpt-oss-120b to CPU router, merged 9/30 16:01Z, first in the 10/01 package) is a different change and coincides with the AMD prefill drop 1141.6 -> 1042.8 tok/s on 10/01; it is not part of this verdict.
votes.corrected_machine_scope: both, no vendor-specific effect: the generated C++ is identical on Intel and AMD, and both the old fallback latch and the new per-item latch wait through the same readiness_source::atomic -> monitor_and_wait path (RTM xbegin/tpause on Granite Rapids, monitorx/mwaitx on Genoa). The change only alters which word is watched and how many sequential waits the main thread makes; wake latency differences are sub-microsecond per layer on either machine.
votes.corrected_category: moe-routing sync granularity (codegen-only, no kernel or math change)
votes.magnitude_estimate: no. Bound: at most ~0.5% worst case (10 us x 36 layers on a 65 ms decode step), realistic <0.1% on decode and ~0.01% on prefill; the first package containing it (2026.09.30) shows Intel decode -0.6% and prefill +0.3%, both inside the +/-0.8% night-to-night spread.

survivors.title: Build MoE slot items with expand_expert_pairs
survivors.author: mitchelldalvirosen-positron
survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-10-02 (d678934166). h/tron/models/feed_forward.hpp: the hand-written MoE batch constructor's inline loop building `slot_items` is replaced by `expand_expert_pairs<n_routed_experts_chosen>(items)`, which generated plugins already use (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:2883). Runs once per batch construction, not per layer. PR body: 'behavior-preserving refactor.' Same item order, same size; no measurable change expected. Only the hand-written MoE model (mixtral) is affected.

votes.reason: The code path is reachable in the nightly rinzler, but the change is a byte-for-byte equivalent refactor with no performance effect. Evidence: merge d678934166 (2026-10-02 16:36 UTC) touches only h/tron/models/feed_forward.hpp (+1/-11). The mixture_of_experts::batch constructor's inline lambda (reserve items.size()*K, nested loop, push_back(token_slot_t(token, slot_id(slot)))) is replaced by expand_expert_pairs<n_routed_experts_chosen>(items) [h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp:300], whose body is the same reserve, the same loop order, and emplace_back(token, slot_id(slot)). token_slot_t is an alias for token_slot_id<n_routed_experts_chosen> [feed_forward.hpp:174], so the vector type is identical. Reachability: feed_forward.hpp is included only by h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp (the hand-written plugin); mixtral_8x7b is config/models.yaml 'source: hand_authored' with production/test tags, and mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1-tp2 appears in 39 nightly rows on both intel and amd. No env flag or build option gates the path. The other MoE row (ingested-gpt-oss-120b-tp4) is a generated plugin that already called expand_expert_pairs (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:2827), so it is unaffected. Timing: merged 2026-10-02, ten days after the 9/22 boost window, so it cannot explain that step. Nightly mixtral intel decode tps_mean around the merge: 80.79 (10/01), 80.88 (10/02), 80.67 (10/03), 80.68 (10/04); prefill 812/804/813/815 tok/s. No step.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no. The constructor builds a vector of n_tokens*2 small ids once per batch (per decode step), est. well under 1 us against a step time of about 12 ms at 80 tok/s; both before and after code do the same reserve and loop, and nightly mixtral tps_mean is flat across 10/01-10/04 (80.79 -> 80.68).

votes.reason: The diff is one file, h/tron/models/feed_forward.hpp (+1/-11). It replaces an inline lambda that builds `slot_items` with a call to `expand_expert_pairs<n_routed_experts_chosen>(items)` [h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp:300-308]. Both versions do the same work: reserve items.size()*n_routed_experts_chosen, then a nested loop over tokens and slots that appends `token_slot_id<n_routed_experts_chosen>(token, slot_id(slot))` in the same order (push_back of a temporary vs emplace_back, same trivially-copyable element type, since `token_slot_t` is an alias for `token_slot_id<n_routed_experts_chosen>` [feed_forward.hpp:174]). The resulting vector is identical in type, size and order, so the downstream channels (w1o, w3o, acto, w2o) see the same item list. The code runs once per MoE batch-object construction, not per layer or per token, and costs on the order of items*k small struct appends (a few hundred elements for mixtral's k=2). This cannot move decode TPS or prefill of any nightly row by 1%. It also merged 2026-10-02, ten days after the 9/22 boost onset, so it cannot explain a change that began on 9/22. The change touches only the hand-written MoE plugin (mixtral); generated plugins already used expand_expert_pairs. Nothing in it is machine-specific (no AMX, no timed-wait, no SIMD path), so Intel vs AMD behavior is the same.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no: identical vector built by identical loop (same reserve, order, element type), executed once per batch construction, est. microseconds per batch; far below 1% of decode or prefill time, and merged 2026-10-02, after the 9/22 window.

survivors.title: Move GPT-OSS-120B to the CPU router
survivors.author: rbjarnason-positron
survivors.evidence: Merged 2026-09-30 16:01 UTC (43e533f7b6). config/models.yaml adds 'moe_router: cpu' to ingested_gpt_oss_120b, so the generated 120B plugin compiled into the .deb now runs the MoE router (gate matmul + top-4) on the CPU in BF16 instead of INT4 on the FPGA. PR body claims: 'With 4 and 8 users on 4 cards, time to first token is 2.5–2.9% shorter. With one user, decode is 0.9–1.2% slower.' Table: 4 cards 4 users decode 'no change (noise)', 8 users decode '0.8% faster (noise)', total output rate '1.9% higher' at 8 users; 'The single-user decode loss appears in all six pairs at both card counts, about 30–70 µs per token.' Direction depends on the CI row's user count: prefill slightly faster, decode flat to slightly slower. This is a 9/30 change, so it cannot explain a boost that started on 9/22. Applies equally on Intel and AMD.

votes.reason: Not refuted: the change reaches the nightly 120B row. Chain verified on origin/main (the local HEAD 3b16a74966 is a 9/29 checkout that predates the merge, so I read origin/main 95f5c45931): config/models.yaml:672 sets `moe_router: cpu` on ingested_gpt_oss_120b -> config/model_definitions.py write_ingest_cmake emits populate_ingest_model(... "cpu") -> ingest/CMakeLists.txt:389-439 passes `--moe-router cpu` to ingest/build-model.py -> the Haskell generator (TypedFxBulk.hs MoeRouterCpu, Note [MoE router placement policy]) lowers the gate to a host `matvec` fused into one per-token router kernel (TronCpp.hs:2276) instead of an FPGA Matmul. The nightly golden benchmark (.github/workflows/benchmark-golden.yml) builds runtron from source at the workflow sha with `make gen/config/test` (test profile, BUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON; the 120B variant is tagged production,test,core), so the regenerated plugin is in the binary. The CI row is bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py STANDARD_JOBS: model=ingested-gpt-oss-120b, tensor_parallel=4, instances_to_use=2, prompts_to_use=8 (4 users per 4-card instance), prompt 2047, gen 514, matching the PR's "4 cards, 4 users" table (TTFT 2.5-2.9% shorter, decode "no change (noise)"). The host kernel is h/tron/kernels/host_matvec.hpp using _mm512_dpbf16_ps (AVX-512 BF16), not AMX, so it behaves the same on delphi and andoria. Timing: merged 2026-09-30 16:01 UTC, so first visible in the 10/01 nightly; it cannot explain a boost starting 9/22 and does not touch any other model.
corrected_models: ingested-gpt-oss-120b (tp4 row, 2 instances x 4 users, prompt 2047 / gen 514)
votes.magnitude_estimate: Prefill: yes (est. 2.5-2.9% shorter TTFT at 4 users on 4 cards per the PR's own paired runtron medians, same shape as the CI row). Decode: no (PR reports "no change (noise)" at 4 users; the 0.9-1.2% loss is single-user only). Both apply only from the 10/01 nightly onward and only to the 120B row.

votes.reason: The diff is exactly as flagged: config/models.yaml adds `moe_router: cpu` to ingested_gpt_oss_120b (one line), plus test and README updates [config/models.yaml:651 in 43e533f7b6]. That flag changes the generated 120B plugin, so every build after 2026-09-30 16:01 UTC runs the MoE gate matmul and top-4 selection on the CPU in BF16 instead of INT4 on the FPGA. The PR's own paired measurements (median of six runtron pairs, 2048-token prompt, 512 generated tokens) put the effect at or above the 1% line: time to first token 1.0% shorter (2 cards, 1 user) and 2.5-2.9% shorter (4 cards, 4 and 8 users); single-user decode 0.9-1.2% slower in all six pairs (30-70 us per token). So it can plausibly move the gpt-oss-120b-tp4 nightly row by >=1%, in opposite directions for prefill (faster) and decode (slower). It cannot explain a decode boost that started 9/22: it merged 9/30 and its decode effect is a loss, not a gain. Machine scope: the CPU router kernel does not use AMX. In this tree AMX appears only in src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp (the attention kernel), so the router matmul runs on ordinary AVX code on both Granite Rapids and Genoa. The effect should be of similar size on both machines, with no AMX-dependent difference. Only ingested-gpt-oss-120b (tp2 and tp4 variants) is touched; gpt-oss-20b and qwen3-30b already used the CPU router since #4367.
votes.magnitude_estimate: yes - PR's own paired measurements: prefill (time to first token) 1.0-2.9% shorter, single-user decode 0.9-1.2% slower (30-70 us/token), on gpt-oss-120b only, from 9/30 onward; decode direction is a loss, so it cannot be the 9/22 boost.

dropped.title: prequant: Separate weight DMA submission from completion

votes.reason: Merge 95ee5ea9f4 (2026-09-24) touches six files. Only two reach the real driver: h/libpos.hpp:519 and src/pos/driver.cpp:1004 drop `TRON(noescape)` (expands to `__attribute__((noescape))` under clang-19, h/common/attributes.hpp:642) from the `qdata` parameter of `xfer_blocks`. That function is reachable in production rinzler (FPGA-attention KV upload at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1014/:1142 and src/pos/hwattention.cpp:62, weight load at driver.cpp:1484), but the change is a declaration-only optimizer hint removal: no instruction in the DMA submission path changes, the pointer is handed to hardware descriptors regardless, and the previous attribute was already incorrect (the pointer does escape), so the generated code for the submission loop is the same modulo caller-side alias assumptions. The remaining files are not in the deb build: src/pos/fake.cpp and h/pos/fake_instrumentation.hpp belong to the `pos_fake` static library (src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:44-69, FAKE_DEVICE), t/t_prequant_cache.cpp is a test (ENABLE_TESTS=OFF in the deb preset), and h/tron/hardware/weight_transfer.hpp has no includer anywhere in h/ or src/ (grep returns nothing; the PR body itself defers its callers to #4011/#4012). No reachable runtime path exists that could change decode or prefill throughput for any nightly model.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no - removing a noescape attribute from one pointer parameter of a DMA-submission function cannot raise throughput; the DMA and hardware wait dominate that path, and no production caller of the new weight_transfer.hpp helpers exists in the tree.

votes.reason: Verified in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-main-ro (merge 95ee5ea9f4, 2026-09-24). The diff touches 6 files. Only two lines reach the real rinzler binary: removing TRON(noescape) from the qdata parameter of xfer_blocks in h/libpos.hpp:519 and src/pos/driver.cpp:1004. The other four files are the fake backend (src/pos/fake.cpp, h/pos/fake_instrumentation.hpp, built as the separate static library pos_fake in src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:44, not linked into the real driver), a test (t/t_prequant_cache.cpp), and the new header h/tron/hardware/weight_transfer.hpp, which at merge time was included only by that test (git grep at 95ee5ea9f4); its first production include arrived with PR #4011 on 2026-09-29, so any effect of that header belongs to #4011, and even there it is weight-load time, not decode or prefill. The compiler is clang-19 (CMakePresets.json:19), so the attribute was live: tron_noescape expands to __attribute__((noescape)) (h/common/attributes.hpp:641). That attribute only lets the optimizer in the callers assume the buffer pointer is not captured after the call. The callers are the KV upload paths (h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1014 and :1142, src/pos/hwattention.cpp:62) and weight load (src/pos/driver.cpp:1484). In each, the pointer is a heap DMA buffer passed into xfer_blocks inside a per-fetcher loop, so the worst-case codegen difference is a few extra pointer reloads per call (nanoseconds) against a call that writes DMA descriptors over MMIO (microseconds) inside a decode step measured in milliseconds. The annotation was also semantically wrong (the DMA engine reads qdata after xfer_blocks returns, per branch commit 90edcce348 "Stop claiming asynchronous DMA sources do not escape"), so removing it can only remove a latent miscompile, not change speed. The PR body contains no measured performance claim; the "DMA latency vs DMA bandwidth" sentence describes future callers (#4011, #4012). The TRON(noescape) still visible on set_hardware_weights (driver.cpp:1471 on origin/main) is a different function and unchanged by this PR.
votes.corrected_machine_scope: both (compiled into every rinzler build on both machines, zero measurable effect on either; nothing touches AMX, RTM or MWAITX paths, so no Intel-vs-AMD difference)
votes.corrected_category: non-runtime: compiler-annotation removal + fake-backend + unused header (not kv-cache)
votes.magnitude_estimate: no - the only real-hardware change is dropping an optimizer hint on one DMA-submission parameter; worst case is a few nanoseconds of extra pointer reloads per xfer_blocks call versus microsecond MMIO descriptor writes inside millisecond decode steps, far below 1% for decode TPS or prefill on any listed row.

votes.reason: Refuted by a regenerated-code diff. The Haskell ingest tool (the code generator that turns a Torch trace into a C++ model plugin) was built at the parent of the merge (506eeeadfb, pre-PR) and at the merge commit a1c8a51913 (post-PR), in worktrees /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/pr3660-regen and /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/pr3660-regen-post. Both binaries were run on the same traces (/home/jhan/workspace/tron-amx/ingest/traces/ingested-gpt-oss-120b and .../ingested-meta-models-Muse-Glimmer-30B) with the registry settings (gpt-oss-120b: --moe-router cpu, --target-executor plain). The generated plugins are byte-identical: ingested_gpt_oss_120b.hpp md5 e70a4b2856f5dd5326d2cc4f0d6a3903 before and after, ingested_meta_models_Muse_Glimmer_30B.hpp md5 ba54c9e86fc117adc4cb3271718865db before and after (outputs in .../pr3660-regen/out-pre and .../pr3660-regen-post/out-post). Why nothing changes: the new lowering paths only fire when (a) a pointwise expert body reads the token-indexed shared activation (emits ix.token()) or (b) a MoeView is consumed directly by MoeBlend (adds a 'moe_view' copy kernel). gpt-oss-120b's MoE body (root_moe_body_*.fx) is hidden[token_indices] -> mm(gate_up) -> +bias -> pointwise on the matmul output -> mm(down) -> +bias -> blend, so the MoeView feeds only a MoeMatmul, which keeps the pre-existing zero-copy token-slot view. Muse-Glimmer-30B is not an MoE model at all: its generated plugin has n_routed_experts = 0 and its trace metadata has no expert fields, so no MoE view exists. Dense CI models (qwen3-4b, gemma-4-31b) have no MoE views either. The runtime side is unaffected: the PR touches only ingest/ (26 files, all Haskell/Python codegen and tests); no src/ C++, no rinzler, no CMake preset. Reachability facts that were checked and would otherwise have made the PR live: the nightly deb (publish-deb.yml, 01:17 UTC) runs 'make deb', which configures with -DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE="" and BUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON, so plugins ARE regenerated from the Haskell tool at every build; and the first package containing this merge is 2026.10.04-fb3c50e3 (head 2026-10-03T18:50Z), so only the 10/04 nightly row, not 10/03, could have seen it (packages.json new_prs lists 3660 only for that package). Both conditions hold, yet the regenerated code is identical, so the nightly binary for the listed models is unchanged by this PR. Caveat: the traces used were exported 2026-09-11 by the tron-amx checkout; ingest/export changed between then and the merge, but the gpt-oss MoE body pattern that decides which lowering path is taken is architecture-defined and did not change.
votes.magnitude_estimate: no — the generated C++ for ingested-gpt-oss-120b and ingested-meta-models--Muse-Glimmer-30B is byte-identical before and after the PR, and no runtime (src/) file changed, so decode and prefill of every listed row are unaffected (0% by construction).

votes.reason:
Short version: the merge reached only the 10/04 nightly, the two CI MoE models do not take any of the changed lowering paths, and the 10/04 CI rows show no change beyond run-to-run noise.

Exposure window (corrects the first pass): a1c8a51913 was merged 2026-10-03 13:00 UTC. The 10/03 nightly package 2026.10.03-4c2c42ab is built from 4c2c42ab72, merged 2026-10-02 22:45 UTC, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says it does NOT contain #3660. The 10/04 package 2026.10.04-fb3c50e3 (fb3c50e3b2, 2026-10-03 18:50 UTC) is the first and only nightly that contains it. The PR cannot explain anything observed 9/22 through 10/03.

Code path (structural argument from the diff and the exporters): the generated C++ for an ingested MoE model changes only if (a) a MoeView output is read by a pointwise expert kernel (new `ix.token()` projection, KernelTokenIndexExpr), (b) a MoeView output is consumed directly by MoeBlend (new `moe_view` copy par-kernel), (c) an expert-pairs par kernel reads a QBatchItems channel (new `start_reading_at(loopvar.token())`), or (d) one channel has parallel readers over both QBatchItems and QBatchItemsExpertPairs (new normalizeConsumers/consumerCompatible branches). In the exported expert bodies, the gathered token rows feed only matmuls: gpt-oss (ingest/export/gpt_oss_export.py expert_body) does `hidden_selected = hidden[token_indices]` and its only use is `hidden_selected @ gate_up_w_i`; the bias add, clamps and GLU operate on the matmul output in slot space. The shared Qwen3-MoE body (ingest/export/moe_export.py routed_gated_mlp, registered for Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock) does `selected = hidden[token_indices]` and uses it only in `selected @ gate_w_i.t()` and `selected @ up_w_i.t()`. For a MoeView consumed by MoeMatmul, the new BulkLoopy MoeMatmul case returns the backing array name for a TokenOfSlot view over a QBatchItems array, which is the same name the old transparent alias produced, and TronCpp's moeMatmulPrepareAndLaunch (the token_slot_view wrapping) is untouched by the PR. For llama-3.1-8b that is 224 increments per forward, about 22 us est. (at ~100 ns per cross-core RMW) against a 7.7 ms decode forward, about 0.3%. The ~batch() wait checks the condition before entering the Intel RTM/tpause or AMD mwaitx branch (src/system/mwaitx.cpp for_event_cycles), so it is a single load when the count is already zero. The count is already zero in decode and in any pass that emits logits, because run_logits waits on logits_done (model.hpp:3280) and the PR body states the logits callback is queued behind every layer callback on the RX thread. Only a no-logits prefill chunk can leave a few last-layer channel-release callbacks outstanding; that wait is bounded by RX dispatch latency (microseconds) against a prefill forward of tens to hundreds of ms. PR body ABAB on andoria-08 (llama-3.1-8b TP1): +0.9% at 1 user, -0.3% at 4 users, both inside the 0.3-0.6% A/A spread and under one SD (2.4 tok/s). ## 3. Phase order and the effect of failure or cancellation

Order, each phase wrapped in its own try/except so a crash does not skip later phases [scripts/system_ci.py:794-795]:

```
functional [797-819] -> perf [821-848] -> MMLU [850-876] -> soak [878-979]
```

- Perf is called with `raise_for_goal=False` [system_ci.py:829], so perf results never raise inside the phase.
- A functional test *failure* (pytest exit code != 0) is logged and counted, not raised [system_ci.py:590-593]. Nothing is done to the DUT. Perf then provisions its own model per row [perf.py:347].
- A functional *crash* (Python exception) calls `check_dut_health("functional")` [system_ci.py:814-816], which since 57189c1 (09-21 head, first ran 09-22) calls `dut.recover_inference_after_failure()` [system_ci.py:774; inventory.py:290-307]: legacy mode waits for platformd idle; explicit mode deletes the harness-owned engines and proxy. Before 09-22 it only waited for idle. Either way perf then re-provisions from a clean state. This does not change how perf measures.
- "failure" status on Intel: the entry point `system_ci` is `scripts.system_ci:main` since a98573c [pyproject.toml:45]; `main` returns 1 when `enforce_report` raises `SystemCiFailed` because the effective threshold verdict is not PASSED [system_ci.py:431-435, 635-642]. Before a98573c the same exception propagated uncaught, also giving a non-zero exit. So "failure" = thresholds not met or report incomplete, evaluated *after* all four phases. It says nothing about the perf phase's state.
- "cancelled" status on AMD 09-26..29: the job limit was `timeout-minutes: 720` (12 h) until 7dd141e8 raised it to 960 on 09-29 [system_ci_genoa96_rinzler.yaml:8]. On timeout GitHub sends SIGTERM; `_handle_sigterm` publishes partial reports from `_sigterm_state["perf_results"]` and exits 143 [system_ci.py:493-551]. Perf samples are written to Talos during `test_performance` itself [perf.py:421-438], before MMLU and the 3 h soak start [system_ci_genoa96_rinzler.yaml:24], so a timeout during MMLU/soak leaves perf data complete. The reason the AMD run exceeded 12 h on those nights is not recorded in the harness commits (1fb671f has no body). `Insufficient data`; the per-phase `test_suite_duration` samples in Talos for those sessions would show which phase grew.
- Note the DUT update step: every night, before `uv run system_ci`, the workflow runs `apt-get remove tron; apt-get install tron; apt-get upgrade -y` on the DUT [both yamls:46-50]. The tron build and all other packages on the DUT therefore change nightly outside this repo; that is where an AMX enablement or other tuning would arrive.

candidates.author: jhan-positron

The deb preset now compiles kernels/amx_attn.cpp and the gate amx_eligible (head 128, kv_mul 4) && amx_attn_h128g4::available() is true only on the Intel CPU [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1440-1443]. The row moved +15.0% decode (28.25 -> 32.49 TPS, 320 samples, sd 0.16 TPS) and the same-code AMX on/off A/B on 09-20 measured +14.0% on that row; the AMD row stayed flat (29.00 -> 28.91). The +61% prefill on that row (prompt 4096, 32 users) is attention-dominated and fits the same cause. Plausible for llama-3.3-70b tp4 +3.1% if its shard geometry meets the gate (Insufficient data: the geometry per shard was not read). It cannot explain gpt-oss-120b (head 64, FPGA attention). For qwen-3-4b (head 128, kv_mul 4, FPGA attention in the nightly) a software prefill and decode-tail path exists, so AMX cannot be excluded there without a TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 A/B. candidates.title: Disable wait statistics by default
candidates.author: rbjarnason-positron
candidates.why: Strongest candidate for the Intel-biased, non-AMX part of the step (qwen-3-4b tp4 +18.9% decode, gpt-oss-120b +9.3% decode, qwen tp2 +9.6% prefill). Before this PR every timed wait did count_calls++ once and count_waits++ once per loop iteration on two process-wide std::atomic<int> that share one cache line [git diff eeb72c0348^1 eeb72c0348 -- src/system/mwaitx.cpp]. The loop iteration rate differs by machine: on Intel the RTM path returns after tsx_pause_budget = 2048 TSC cycles (about 0.76 us) so every idle thread hits the shared line about 1.3 million times per second [src/system/mwaitx.cpp:128,171-180]; on AMD mwaitx sleeps up to the full remaining timeout, so one increment per wait [src/system/mwaitx.cpp:133-150]. The FPGA rx poll uses a 2000 ns timed wait [src/pos/worker.cpp:164], so FPGA workers were the main contributors. With 288 logical CPUs on delphi the cache-line traffic is far larger than on andoria. The author measured +6.94% (4 users) and +11.25% (1 user) decode on GPT-OSS-20B from removing only the counters, on AMD. Merged 6 minutes after #4505 and shipped in the same first package, so the two are inseparable in CI data. Weakness: the mechanism touches every model's thread pool, yet seven Intel rows did not move; the data cannot say why only FPGA-attention rows (and the AMX row) responded. The tightened within-run spread on qwen tp4 (slow tail removed) is more consistent with removed contention than with a faster kernel.
candidates.machine_scope: both, Intel-biased (RTM path increments the shared counter ~13x more often per wait than the AMD mwaitx path)

attributions.non_pr_explanations:
Short version: no PR in the 2026.09.29 package has a mechanism for an Intel-only, cross-model decode step, and the same .deb left AMD flat, so the cause is most likely on the delphi machine. One machine-side event sits exactly between the two nightlies and fits the pattern; it is not yet confirmed.

1. platformd restart and FPGA re-enumeration on delphi (leading explanation, unconfirmed). Evidence for: platformd (the daemon that programs and manages the FPGA cards and writes the rinzler unit environment) was started manually at 2026-09-28 23:54:37 UTC; all 8 FPGA PCI devices and their vfio nodes were re-created at 2026-09-29 00:03:50 UTC; bringup-done at 00:03:59 UTC; the 09-28 nightly ended 05:28 UTC and the 09-29 nightly began 04:05 UTC, so this is the only delphi event between them (machine-state agent). The FPGA bitfile packages had been upgraded 2026-09-25 03:42 UTC (archer-ia860m 1.5.8.0 -> 1.5.9.0) but cards keep the image they were programmed with until the next bringup, so 09-29 is plausibly the first nightly on the new image. The step shape matches an FPGA-side or host-to-card-path change rather than a CPU-code change: every row whose decode step is dominated by FPGA weight streaming moved by a similar 1-2.5% (70b, qwen-2.5-32b, mixtral, gemma, gpt-oss), the two 32-user rows that are CPU-attention bound did not move (llama-3.1-8b 32u +0.1%, llama-3.2-3b 32u +0.2%), and the largest move is gpt-oss prefill +8.5%, which runs FPGA attention and FPGA MoE matmuls. Evidence against / gaps: the platformd journal for 23:54-00:04 UTC was not readable (no adm/systemd-journal membership), so whether the bringup activated 1.5.9.0, changed card clocks, or changed the rinzler environment is Insufficient data. A fresh bringup could also have re-trained a PCIe link or re-placed DMA host buffers; the step persisting 6 nights argues for a persistent state change (image version, link state, config) rather than a transient fresh-boot effect.

2. AMD comparison. On andoria the same .deb produced no 09-29 step on any row (all 11 clean rows within pre-period scatter; the 09-29 anomalies are the known slow-card bitfile incidents). AMD gpt-oss decode did move +3.0% from 09-30 (124.9 -> 128.6 TPS) with no other AMD row moving; Slack attributes it to a bitfile action on that machine (Rhys). That is a second example of a card-side event moving an FPGA-bound row by a few percent while the software was unchanged, but its pattern (one row) differs from delphi's (all 4u/8u rows), so it supports only the general mechanism, not the specific cause.

3. Software toolchain: flake.lock, CMakePresets.json, cmake/, packaging/ and all CMakeLists.txt are unchanged between ee2d5be0 and 7e5085ed; only flake.nix (Perfetto pins, patched Ninja) and gcp-nix.yml changed. No compiler or flag change, so no codegen difference. A toolchain change would also move AMD, which did not happen.

4. Harness: the harness agent found no measurement, load, prompt or order change for pre-existing rows in the window (perf_metrics.py untouched; tps.py capture window and formulas identical). The 09-29 nightly ran 04:05-05:22 UTC vs 04:10-05:28 UTC the night before, same slot.

5. Earlier PR candidates already in the tree (#4534 wait statistics, #4505 AMX, #4258, #4353) shipped on 09-23/09-24 and are present in both the 09-28 and 09-29 packages, so they cannot produce a 09-28 -> 09-29 step. #4713 (CPU router) and #4654 are in the 09-30 or 10-01 packages, after the step.

6. Timing/thermal: the nightly logs carry card power and temperature samples (seen in the soak-phase log excerpt cardblock_0925.txt), but nobody has compared 09-28 vs 09-29 card telemetry yet. Insufficient data.
attributions.what_would_isolate:
Two measurements, in order of cost.

A. Package-vs-machine A/B on delphi-3bda (under the CI lease rules): on the current card state, install the 2026.09.28-ee2d5be0 .deb and run four nightly rows with the harness as the nightly does them (llama-3.3-70b-instruct-good-tp2 8 users, qwen-2.5-32b-it-fast-tp2 8 users, gemma-2-9b-it-fast-tp2 8 users, ingested-gpt-oss-120b-tp4 8 users for the prefill signal), then install 2026.09.29-7e5085ed and repeat back-to-back, 3 runs each, no other change. If the 09-28 .deb now gives the post-step numbers (about 17.0, 36.0, 104.1 TPS and gpt-oss prefill about 1062 tok/s) the step is machine state, not the package; if it gives the pre-step numbers (16.6, 35.3, 102.8, 982) the package is the cause and the 13 PRs need a bisect. Pre-period scatter is 0.1-0.7% per row, so 3 runs per arm resolve a 1.1% step.

B. Confirm the machine-side event (read-only, needs journal access): `journalctl -u platformd --since 2026-09-28T23:50 --until 2026-09-29T00:05` on delphi for image-activation lines and the activated image version; read the currently programmed image version from each card via platformd/tron tooling and compare with the version platformd logged at the 2026-09-21 19:58 UTC bringup; `lspci -vv -s <card>` LnkSta for all 8 cards (Gen/width) now, and `find /opt/positron/config.d /etc/positron -newermt 2026-09-28T20:00 ! -newermt 2026-09-29T04:00` for a config edit by the 23:11 UTC login. Also diff the card power/temperature/clock telemetry blocks of the 09-28 and 09-29 nightly logs (the format in cardblock_0925.txt): a step in card power at equal load would point at a clock or image change. If the bringup is confirmed to have activated 1.5.9.0, the decisive test is a same-.deb run on the previous image (1.5.8.0 is still installed under /opt/positron/images/archer-ia860m-es-standard) versus the current image.

attributions.non_pr_explanations: 1) FPGA bitfile 1.5.9.0 activation (strong, see candidate 0): evidence for = 13/13 night state match on andoria, same-size Intel step on 09-29 when delphi activated the same image, co-occurrence of the 1.5.9-specific slow-card defect only on high-state nights, apt log lines (install 09-25 03:09:57Z; '1.5.9.0 over 1.5.8.0' re-install 10-01 03:14:45Z proving a rollback; 'kept back' 10-03/10-04), Rhys's 10-02 09:33 PDT description of the reset-service mechanism. Evidence against = none found; the only gap is that the per-card image version was not printed by the nightly logs (Insufficient data: platformd journal / pho card report on andoria-b1a3 for 09-26 ~03:3x UTC and 10-02 would make it direct). 2) Cancelled workflows / longer perf phase on 09-26..29 (rejected as cause): per-row durations from runs.json show only the slow-card rows stretched (09-26 70b-tp4 11 -> 46 min; 09-29 70b-tp2 8u 16 -> 71 min, 4u 10 -> 60 min, gpt-oss 4 -> 40 min), all other rows kept 2-16 min; the runs were killed at 15:10 UTC by the 12 h limit during soak (log tails), after perf had completed; high state also occurs on 09-30 (normal 6.0 MB run) and 10-02 (4.6 MB, threshold failure), so cancellation does not track the state. 3) Harness change (rejected): systems_test head 6a38e6e1 for 09-24..09-29 (spans the step); later heads 7dd141e8 (09-30, Genoa96 timeout 16 h), ff8d05d7 (10-01, Glimmer row), b1ccc0b8 (thresholds) touch no measurement code; provisioning mode 'explicit' every night. 4) Tron package 2026.09.26-dbeb404f (rejected): 9 PRs, 7 non-runtime, 2 negligible; Intel ran it on 09-26 with no row moving >0.5%; later packages (10-01, 10-03, 10-04) ran in the low state, so no software in the deb can be the carrier. 5) Time-of-day / thermal (no evidence): 10-04 started 04:38Z (an hour late) and was low state; 10-02 started 03:42Z and was high state. 6) gpt-oss-120b decode is the one row that does not follow the bitfile: it rose on 09-30 (125 -> 128.8) and stayed high on 1.5.8.0 nights; that is a separate step (packages 09-30/10-01, e.g. #4713 CPU router merged 09-30 16:01Z is in the 10-01 package) and is outside this attribution.
attributions.what_would_isolate: A/B/A on andoria-b1a3 with one tron deb held fixed (e.g. 2026.10.04-fb3c50e3) and the nightly rows re-run three times in the same harness: (A) cards on 1.5.8.0 as now (apt-mark hold in place), (B) apt-get install archer-ia860m-es-standard=1.5.9.0 && sudo rm /run/platformd/bringup-done && sudo systemctl restart platformd, confirm all 8 cards report 01.05.09.00 via pho, re-run, (A') roll back and re-run. Use llama-3.3-70b tp2 8u (sd 0.01 TPS; expect 17.59 vs 18.11, +3.0%), mixtral 8u (77.8 vs 79.0) and qwen-2.5 8u (37.56 vs 38.18) as the cleanest rows, and gpt-oss tp4 TTFT for prefill (expect ~1.0k vs ~1.14k tok/s). Expected: B differs from A and A' by the step size, with no tron change. Same A/B/A on delphi-3bda would confirm the Intel 09-29 step (70b tp2 8u 16.61 vs 17.02). Without a run, read platformd's journal on andoria-b1a3 (journalctl -u platformd --since 2026-09-26T00:00 --until 2026-09-26T04:00, and the same for 2026-10-02) for the image-activation line, which pins the card image per nightly directly.
